title: Where Do Legal Factors Live in LLMs?
abstract: arXiv:2610.28799v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In case-based legal reasoning, legal professionals identify legally significant fact patterns in a new dispute and compare them with those of decided cases. In AI & Law, HYPO dimensions and CATO factors represent these patterns symbolically, organizing expert knowledge distilled from case narratives as explicit, structured, interpretable, and auditable legal concepts and relations that support case comparison, legal argument, and precedent-based reasoning. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for legal tasks, yet their internal organization of legal knowledge remains difficult to trace. We investigate whether LLMs form internal representations corresponding to all 26 CATO factors. Two research questions examine linear decodability and sparse localization with sparse autoencoders. Experiments cover three open models, Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-2 2B, supported by cross-model comparison and human audit of controlled natur

translated_title: 法律因素在大语言模型中的何处栖身？
translated_abstract: 在基于案例的法律推理中，法律专业人士会在新的争议中识别具有法律意义的事实模式，并将其与已决案件的事实模式进行比较。在人工智能与法律领域，HYPO维度和CATO因素以符号化方式表示这些模式，将从案例叙事中提炼的专家知识组织为显式、结构化、可解释且可审计的法律概念与关系，从而支持案例比较、法律论证以及基于先例的推理。大语言模型（LLM）正日益被用于法律任务，但其法律知识的内部组织方式仍难以追溯。我们研究LLM是否形成了与全部26个CATO因素相对应的内部表征。两个研究问题分别考察线性可解码性，以及利用稀疏自编码器实现的稀疏定位。实验涵盖三个开源模型——Qwen3-1.7B、Qwen3-8B和Gemma-2 2B，并通过跨模型比较以及对受控自然语言文本的人工审计加以支撑。
tldr: 该研究首次验证大语言模型内部形成了与全部26个CATO法律因素相对应的内部表征，并通过线性探测和稀疏自编码器在多个开源模型中实现了对这些法律因素的解码与稀疏定位。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that LLMs internally encode representations corresponding to all 26 CATO legal factors, localizing them via linear probing and sparse autoencoders across three open-source models.
